category_title: Toddlers engaging in physical aggression or object-related peer conflicts
minimal_context: The student is interacting with peers and toys during free-play in the nursery.
dialogue:
TUTOR: You can both use the toys during free-play.

STUDENT: (Shifts from parallel play to grabbing a toy from the peer) I want this one!

TUTOR: Please try to get along with each other.

STUDENT: (Looks directly at the adult to attract attention) Help me! Make him give it to me!

TUTOR: Just figure it out together.

STUDENT: (Screams as intensity increases) No, mine! (Shows opposition, pushes the peer, and uses physical aggression to acquire the object)

options.A: Augment tactics through response promotion and disruption, and reallocate responding to options associated with contingent reinforcement during free-play interactions with peers and toys.
options.B: Adopt a non-intrusive 'tutorial' role, listening carefully to the student's needs, observing their potential, tuning into their language, and allowing the student to explore and make mistakes during free-play.
options.C: Before free-play begins, show the student a brief video clip and discuss how peers respectfully talk to one another, compliment one another, and ask to help each other.
options.D: Implement a program to encourage 'tootling' by providing a collective reward for the peer group when they reach a target number of reports of prosocial behavior during free-play.
